item.title: Akai Announces Open-Source MPC Sample Key with Early Developer Access
item.description:
Akai Announces Open-Source MPC Sample Key with Early Developer Access

Akai is previewing an upcoming 37‑key version of its budget‑friendly MPC Sample, called the MPC Sample Key. Although the device has not been formally announced, Akai is already sharing vibe‑coded mods and has committed to an open‑source firmware and early access for developers.

🔍 Overview

  • The MPC Sample Key is an open‑source, 37‑key take on the MPC Sample.
  • It does not include pads; instead, the keys are used to trigger samples.
  • Akai plans to give hackers and custom‑firmware developers early access to the device.

🛠️ Open‑Source Strategy

  • The firmware will be open source and is expected to run a version of the software found on the MPC Sample, with tweaks for a traditional keyboard, pitch wheel, and mod wheel.
  • Akai will provide an SDK and will seed early devices to developers, as explained by CEO Jack O’Donnell to The Verge.

🎹 Device Details

Feature Detail
Keys 37‑key keyboard (open‑source version of MPC Sample)
Pads None (unlike the higher‑end MPC Key 37)
Sample playback Keys trigger samples
Firmware Open‑source, based on MPC Sample software with keyboard, pitch, and mod‑wheel tweaks
Mod support Vibe‑coded mods can add synths such as Native Instruments Massive, virtual‑analog, and FM synths
Custom OS demo A reel shows a completely custom OS running several synths

🎛️ Vibe‑Coded Mod Demonstrations

  • Instagram Reels posted by Akai display mods that add synths, including Native Instruments Massive.
  • Other mods showcase virtual‑analog and FM synthesis capabilities.
  • One reel features a device running a completely custom operating system with “several different synths in it.”
  • Similar community‑built synth features appear on the regular MPC Sample, built by Claude.

🚀 Early Access & Community Plans

  • Akai is explicitly embracing the explosion of hackers and custom firmware developers by providing early access devices.
  • The company plans to open‑source parts of the MPC Sample platform, potentially the entire system.
  • An SDK will accompany the open‑source software to aid developers.

💡 Why It Matters

  • By open‑sourcing the firmware and offering early developer kits, Akai signals a shift toward a more collaborative hardware ecosystem.
  • The vibe‑coded mods demonstrate how the community can extend the instrument far beyond its original sample‑playback purpose, adding full synth engines and even custom operating systems.
  • This approach could set a precedent for other music‑hardware manufacturers to engage directly with the modding community.

#Akai #OpenSource #MusicTech #MPC

Source: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC

item.title: Spotify Removes 50 Million AI-Generated Tracks From User Recommendations
item.description:
Spotify Removes 50 Million AI-Generated Tracks From User Recommendations

Spotify has announced that it removed more than 50 million songs categorized as AI-generated slop or spam from its recommendation system over the past year.

🔍 Overview

Spotify has implemented changes to its music recommendation system to prioritize songs from human artists. The company reports a “marked decrease in listener concerns” regarding the appearance of slop or spam in recommendations since these changes were made. This follows previous efforts last year where the company took down more than 75 million songs identified as spam.

🧩 How it works

To determine if a track is AI-generated slop, Spotify utilizes a combination of the following:

  • Listener engagement and feedback
  • Upload patterns
  • Metadata
  • Third-party AI detection tools

Additionally, Spotify editors maintain a standard where they do not program content identified as slop or spam.

⚙️ Key details

Spotify has introduced specific policies for AI identities:

  • AI Persona Badge: A label for artists using an AI identity who do not represent a real person.
  • Recommendation Policy: Music from AI personas will not be recommended.

💡 Why it matters

Spotify’s approach differs from other streaming platforms handling AI music:

Platform Approach to AI Music
YouTube Music Labels AI songs
Deezer Provides users an option to filter out AI slop
Bandcamp Bans AI music entirely

Despite these restrictions on slop, Spotify is partnering with Believe (an independent music publisher) and Universal Music Group to launch a tool for creating AI music remixes.

#Spotify #AI #MusicStreaming #GenerativeAI

Source: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations

item.title: YouTube adds AI disclosure label to music tracks
item.description:
YouTube adds AI disclosure label to music tracks

YouTube is rolling out a “Made with AI” label for music tracks that were altered or fully generated using generative AI, beginning in the YouTube Music app and later expanding to the main YouTube app.

🔍 Overview

  • The label appears on tracks that were “altered or fully generated” with AI.
  • It mirrors YouTube’s existing process for applying AI labels to videos.
  • The goal is to give listeners clear information about AI‑generated music.

⚙️ How it works

  • Music partners must disclose generative AI use when uploading songs.
  • If no disclosure is provided, YouTube may use “other signals” to decide if a song is AI‑generated.
  • YouTube combines partner disclosures with its own detection tools to identify AI‑generated tracks.
  • When AI played a significant role, a label is shown directly on the player page.
  • Tapping the label opens a simple menu that shares more information.

🚀 Availability

  • The label is rolling out starting today in the YouTube Music app.
  • It will expand to the main YouTube app later.

📊 Industry context

Platform AI Label Action
Spotify Launched a voluntary AI label earlier this year and said it wouldn’t recommend songs from “AI personas.”
Apple Music Reportedly getting an AI tag.
Deezer Added a switch for filtering out AI tracks.
Bandcamp Banned AI music outright earlier this year.

💡 Why it matters

  • YouTube wants it to be as easy as possible for listeners to have the right information and clarity when it comes to the music they listen to.
  • The label helps differentiate AI‑generated content from human‑created music, supporting informed choice.

#YouTube #AI #Music #Labeling

Source: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs

item.title: Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava Details Human-Centered Strategy for Generative AI Music
item.description:
Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava Details Human-Centered Strategy for Generative AI Music

Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava is carefully navigating the integration of generative AI into the music production platform by focusing on tools that keep human creators at the center of the process.

🔍 Overview

Splice is a sample platform that countless producers rely on for one-shots and melodic loops. Audio samples pulled from the service have been used in major hit songs, including Lisa’s “Money” and “Espresso” by Sabrina Carpenter. Under the leadership of CEO Kakul Srivastava, the company has expanded its footprint and overseen new developments in generative AI while maintaining a strict focus on human-centric technology.

⚙️ Key details

  • Human-Centered AI: Splice is focusing on AI products that keep human creators at the center of the creative process. On an episode of Decoder, Srivastava spoke out against “push-button, get-song” generative AI models like those popularized by Suno.
  • Strategic Acquisitions: Splice has expanded its presence under Srivastava’s leadership, which includes acquiring Spitfire Audio and directing the company’s initiatives in generative AI.
  • Executive History: Before joining Splice, Srivastava served in executive roles at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub, and Adobe. She was also on the early team at Tiny Speck, the company that later became Slack.
  • Remote Work Culture: Splice operates as a remote-first organization, meaning the company does not have a traditional physical hallway.
  • Views on Communication: Srivastava has noted that AI emails are “killing conversations,” stating a preference for a well-written document and a real conversation instead.

💡 Why it matters

As AI music tools become more controversial, Splice is deliberately avoiding fully automated music generation. Instead, the company is threading the line by developing tools that support and collaborate with human producers rather than replacing them.

#Splice #GenerativeAI #MusicTech #CreativeAI

Source: Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava thinks AI emails are killing conversations

item.title: Thoughtful Things Launches Engram AI Sampler and Groovebox on Kickstarter
item.description:
Thoughtful Things Launches Engram AI Sampler and Groovebox on Kickstarter

Music startup Thoughtful Things has launched a Kickstarter campaign for Engram, a sampler and groovebox that utilizes AI to process audio and generate new sounds.

🔍 Overview

Engram is designed for experimental sound design and creating uncanny sounds rather than producing radio-ready music. Founder Evan King describes the device as a “field recorder for latent space,” focusing on exploring AI hallucinations and pushing audio models beyond their limits.

🧩 How it works

Unlike cloud-based AI tools, Engram operates without an internet connection. Its technical specifications include:

  • Local Processing: Runs a “tiny AI” locally on the device.
  • Custom Model: Uses an in-house, custom-trained model.
  • Training Data: Models are trained on open datasets containing audio licensed for commercial use (CC-BY or similar). The company states it has not and will not train models on non-commercial, pirated, or stolen data.
  • Circuit Bending: The device allows users to tweak or break its AI models, drawing inspiration from circuit bending.
  • Open Firmware: Thoughtful Things plans to open the firmware to allow users to tweak the system or load custom models.

⚙️ Key details

In a campaign video, founder Evan King demonstrated the device by using his voice to ask for “piano,” resulting in a glitchy, vaguely piano-like sound.

🚀 Availability

Engram is launching with a limited run via Kickstarter:

Item Price/Detail
Kickstarter Pledge $675 (30% discount)
Estimated Retail Price Between $850 and $900

#ThoughtfulThings #Engram #AImusic #Kickstarter #SoundDesign

Source: Engram is a sampler that turns broken AI hallucinations into music

item.title: Sony and Universal Music Group Sue Suno Over v6 Model Training
item.description:
Sony and Universal Music Group Sue Suno Over v6 Model Training

Sony and Universal Music Group (UMG) have filed a lawsuit against Suno, alleging that the company’s new v6 model infringes on their copyrights.

⚖️ Legal Allegations

Sony and UMG, who did not sign licensing agreements with Suno, accuse the company of “model laundering.” The labels argue that:

  • Training a new model on the outputs of an infringing model does not eliminate infringement.
  • Value from copied recordings is passed from infringing models into their outputs, and then into v6.
  • v6 is described in the complaint as “the fruit of the same poisoned tree.”
  • Even models not directly trained on the plaintiffs’ recordings benefit from Suno’s “retained unauthorized copies.”

⚙️ Technical Claims

Sony further alleges that Suno utilized distillation to train v6, claiming it was trained to replicate results from previous “teacher” models created using infringing data. The labels contend that Suno’s models will continue to be built on stolen data unless the company starts from scratch.

🔍 Suno’s Response

Regarding the development of v6, Suno representatives have stated the following:

  • Jack Brody told The Verge it was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data,” which included “user data.”
  • Suno later confirmed to Engadget that this data includes “creations” from users.

#Suno #Copyright #MusicAI #Lawsuit

Source: Sony and UMG are suing Suno again

item.title: Suno Releases v6 AI Music Model with Record Industry Support
item.description:
Suno Releases v6 AI Music Model with Record Industry Support

Suno has launched v6, its first AI music model developed with support from the record industry. The model is being rolled out starting today, and Suno intends to eventually retire its previous models.

🧩 How it works

According to Suno’s Jack Brody, v6 was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data that does not include the same data that our previous models were trained on.”

Training data includes:

  • Content licensed from partners Believe, BMG, and Warner Music Group
  • “User data”

It remains unclear if the training data is completely free of dubiously obtained content.

⚙️ Key details

Suno v6 consists of three different models:

Model Description
v6-mini Available for free to all; focused on fast, resource-light creation. Results are simpler and often contain more artifacts.
v6-wild Designed for “happy accidents and natural imperfections.”
v6 The standard model.

Capabilities and Performance

  • Genre Understanding: All three models show dramatic improvement in understanding genres, accurately capturing the superficial hallmarks of styles such as “krautrock” or “hyperpop.”
  • Multimodal Prompts: Users are no longer limited to text; v6 can create tracks based on video, images, or other audio.
  • Editing and Mashups: Users can now use plain language within a chat to edit specific parts of a song, such as a single lyric or guitar line, without regenerating the entire track. The model can also combine multiple elements from a user’s Suno library into new creations.

Limitations

  • Human Imperfections: The model cannot capture “natural imperfections.” Attempts to produce dissonant, off-key, or out-of-tune results—including “out-of-tune piano played haphazardly”—have failed.
  • Prompt Adherence: v6 may ignore specific prompts, such as requests for “no drums” or “monotone vocals.”
  • AI Artifacts: Vocals in v6 may produce more harsh-edged artifacts common to AI models than those found in v5.

🚀 Availability

Suno v6 starts rolling out today.

#Suno #AImusic #GenerativeAI #MusicIndustry

Source: Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help

item.title: Universal Music Group and ElevenLabs Partner to Launch AI Music Platform
item.description:
Universal Music Group and ElevenLabs Partner to Launch AI Music Platform

Universal Music Group (UMG) announced on Thursday the launch of a new AI-powered platform developed through a multiyear licensing agreement with ElevenLabs, a company specializing in AI voice and music generation.

🔍 Overview

The platform will allow users to utilize UMG’s catalog of licensed music to create:

  • Song remixes
  • Mashups
  • New takes on tracks

⚙️ Key details

  • Artist Participation: Artists can choose whether or not to participate in the platform.
  • Independence: The platform will remain separate from ElevenLabs’ Music API and ElevenMusic generator.
  • Future Development: The partnership includes the development of additional products and fan experiences in coming months and years, though specific details were not provided.

💡 Why it matters

ElevenLabs CEO Mati Staniszewski stated in the press release, “By combining UMG’s global community and rights management expertise, with our AI models and products, we’ll enable artists and songwriters to create powerful new experiences for their fans, and ensure they are fairly compensated.”

🧩 Context

UMG has established multiple AI licensing arrangements:

Partner Status/Detail
ElevenLabs Developing AI music platform
Udio Currently developing AI music platform
Spotify AI licensing deal
Nvidia AI licensing deal
